diagnosticCommits.summary: record the projection's provenance, row translation and raw fov once
make the projection probe capture a complete frame, once
project the point with the renderer's own parameters too
3.6.1c probe temporal consistency, same-frame pairing, 8 AABB corners, sensitivity scoring, throttled search (uncommitted, awaiting review)

chain.evidence: rebuilds from getRenderPositionComponent()->mPosition, not from the component's raw min/max; players subtract PLAYER_HEIGHT (1.62f, the eye height) so the box lands at the feet
chain.note: the 1.62 subtraction applies only when isPlayer(); if that assumption is wrong on this build, player boxes shift by exactly 1.62 blocks while mob boxes stay correct
same space as the AABB only if LevelRendererPlayer stores an absolute position; a render-relative origin here would put every box off by the render origin

vtable_accessor_scan.method: disassemble the first instructions of all 470 ClientInstance vtable slots and look for the displacement in the body
vtable_accessor_scan.interpretation: every ClientInstance member the SDK already relies on has a virtual accessor; 0x358 and 0x368 have none, so these offsets were found structurally, not through the game's own interface

chain.acceptance_test: isCameraBasis(): three columns unit length and mutually orthogonal; checks the 3x3 only, never the translation
chain.bug: source 0 and source 3 are accepted/kept without forcing w == 0, while the rows are dotted against a point the caller already made camera-relative
chain.additional: the entire fallback chain lives inside `if (auto* rot = player->getActorRotationComponent())`; when that component is missing the chain never runs and viewSource stays 3
chain.status: STATIC VERIFIED (the inconsistency) / UNVERIFIED (whether the game matrix actually carries w)

chain.conversion: toFactor(): (0.1,10) treated as the multiplier 1/tan(fov/2); (30,130) treated as degrees; otherwise fall back to 70 deg vertical
chain.consumer_contract: OWorldToScreen multiplies the offset by fov.x / fov.y, so it must be 1/tan(hfov/2) and 1/tan(vfov/2)

evidence.vtable_pair: slot 455 = movss xmm0,[rcx+0x720]; ret, slot 456 = movss [rcx+0x720],xmm1; ret, slot 457/458 the same for 0x724 -- a real float property with getter and setter
evidence.who_reads_it: 7 movss sites for 0x720 in the whole .text: the getter, the setter, and five inside a 64-byte struct copy at 0x352B3xx / 0x5EB82F6
evidence.interpretation: no rendering code reads ClientInstance+0x720, so this member is not the value the renderer builds its projection from; using it for projection is unsound if the two can diverge (fov setting, sprinting, spyglass)

chain.dead_alternative: LevelRendererPlayer::getFovX()/getFovY() exist in the SDK and are mapped, but no caller exists anywhere in the tree

parameter_sources.origin: MathUtils::origin -- the static, because the name is unqualified inside a MathUtils member function

chain.note: the production path is MIXED: the matrix comes from the transform, the three projection parameters come from the MathUtils statics. OpenGLGui assigns both sets in the same block today (MathUtils::fov = transform.mFov; MathUtils::origin = transform.mOrigin), so they agree in practice -- but nothing in the type system keeps them equal, and the D3D path never writes the statics. A probe that reads only the transform copies can therefore describe a projection the renderer does not perform.
chain.consequence: the diagnostic now computes the same point twice, once per parameter set, and reports both plus their deltas

chain.formula: rel = pos - origin; x = dot(row0, (rel,1)); y = dot(row1, (rel,1)); z = dot(row2, (rel,1)); reject z>0; sx = W/2 + W/2 * x/(-z) * fov.x; sy = H/2 - H/2 * y/(-z) * fov.y
chain.note: the formula itself is a correct pinhole projection once the requirements hold; the reference implementation reproduces it and passes 35 checks

chain.draw_target: ImGui::GetBackgroundDrawList() in the same ImGui frame
chain.conclusion: viewport and ImGui coordinates share one source; no framebuffer/logical-size mismatch on this path

open_questions.question: does ClientInstance+0x358 hold a view matrix at all, and does it carry translation?
open_questions.answerable_by: matrixSource + basis v0/v1/v2 with v0w/v1w/v2w + mat16 glmColumnMajor
open_questions.calibration: a non-zero w is reported as AFFINE_TRANSLATION_TERM_PRESENT. Double subtraction is only claimed when residualMath = w + dot(axis, mathOrigin) is ~0 on all three rows -- the condition for the matrix having already subtracted the very origin getBoxPoints() subtracts again. residualTransform and verdictIfTransformOrigin are printed as a control only; the verdict never uses them.

open_questions.question: what unit are ClientInstance+0x720/0x724 stored in?
open_questions.answerable_by: ciFovRaw next to ciFovConverted, transformFov and mathFov in the same capture
open_questions.not_answerable_by: a single capture. One sample cannot separate 'a multiplier' from 'degrees that happen to convert to the same factor'; two runs with different in-game FOV settings are required, see diagnostic-probe.md section 4
open_questions.production_note: the projecting path consumes mathFov, so judge proportion with mathFovFactorRatio first; fovFactorRatio is the transform copy and only a control

open_questions.question: is LevelRendererPlayer::getCameraPos absolute or render-relative?
open_questions.answerable_by: playerToCamera in the control capture, plus camera in the matrix capture

open_questions.question: do the MathUtils statics and the transform snapshot agree in a real frame?
open_questions.answerable_by: control line: comparable + originsMatch + fovsMatch, then screenDelta as a sensitivity number only
open_questions.interpretation: originsMatch/fovsMatch false means the probe was previously describing a projection the renderer does not perform. A small or zero screenDelta does NOT prove equality: on the view axis a 30% fov difference still moves the pixel by exactly 0 (reference T13a).

open_questions.question: can the control be measured at all, i.e. is there a point in front of the camera?
open_questions.answerable_by: testPoint source / world / testViewZ / transformTestViewZ, or the explicit 'no usable test point' line
open_questions.failure_mode: the local player's render position sits on the camera plane and is rejected by OWorldToScreen's z>=0 guard, which is how 3.6.1a produced a control that measured nothing
open_questions.note: matrixCaptured and projectionControlCaptured are separate: a scene with no usable point still reports the matrix

open_questions.question: if matrixSource=2, is the synthesised matrix actually correct?
open_questions.answerable_by: not by this probe. Source 2 means viewMatrixFromRotation(yaw, pitch) was adopted, not validated: the yaw/pitch sign convention, the camera direction and the handedness still need independent checks

open_questions.question: are the matrix facts and the control point from the same frame?
open_questions.answerable_by: matrixCaptureFrame / controlCaptureFrame / sameFrame on the paired header
open_questions.guarantee: structural, not statistical: the paired block re-reads matrixSource, origins, fov, mat16, rowW and the affine verdict on the control frame, so it never reuses the preliminary block's numbers. sameFrame only reports whether the two blocks coincide.
open_questions.failure_mode: pairing the preliminary snapshot with a later control point would describe a projection the renderer never performed -- matrix from frame N, point from frame M
